metaData.title: Blue Ridge Beekeepers Federation introductory call

sentences.text: Good afternoon. This is really a call to work out who needs to be in the room rather than to show you anything.
That suits me. I have twenty five minutes and then a call with our regional chairs.
Tell me how a decision like this actually gets made at your federation.
Slowly, and through two committees.
Anything over twenty thousand dollars a year goes to the finance committee first and then to the full board.
Finance meets on the second Tuesday of the month and the board meets quarterly, with the next one on the third of December.
So realistically the December board meeting is the first point a decision could be taken.
It is, and only if finance has seen it in November.
If it misses November it goes to the March board, and nobody wants that because our membership year opens in April.
Then let us work backwards from November. What does the finance committee need in front of them?
A one page summary, a three year cost, and the name of a comparable federation we can telephone.
They will not read anything longer than a page, and I say that with affection.
Who else should be on a demonstration when we get to one?
Myself, our membership secretary, and one of the regional chairs so that the volunteers feel represented.
Our treasurer will want to be there for anything touching money, but he travels a great deal and we work around him.
Four people is a workable number. How long a session would they sit through?
An hour, no more, and preferably in the morning.
Our membership secretary is a volunteer with a day job, so evenings are worse for her than mornings, which surprises people.
Would that be in person or would a video call be acceptable to them?
A video call is fine and frankly better. We are spread across three states and getting four of us in one building takes a month.
We did the whole of our insurance review on video last year and nobody complained.
Then I will hold an hour in the first half of October and send it round for the four of you.
The week of the sixth is better than the week of the thirteenth. Our autumn field day is on the eighteenth and the fortnight before it is chaos.
The week of the sixth then. I will send something over tomorrow with two or three times in it.
Good. And send the one page summary separately, because our membership secretary likes to read before she listens.
Understood. Thank you for the twenty five minutes, that was more useful than a demonstration would have been today.
I thought it might be. Speak in October.
